title: Trapped in Relationships: The Cost of Abuse and Neglect
coreMove: Early abuse can teach the body a map of love, threat, and blame; healing begins by reading that map safely instead of forcing memory or denying the body.

exampleSpecs.audience: survivors hearing a story that resembles their own
exampleSpecs.stakes: recognition arriving too fast for safety
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use a group therapy story to connect childhood incest with terror during sexual intimacy.

exampleSpecs.audience: patients and clinicians separating blame from context
exampleSpecs.stakes: physical illness reduced to a simple trauma claim
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show autoimmune disease and vision loss as medical facts that may still be discussed beside trauma history.

exampleSpecs.audience: adults whose intimacy panic outruns explanation
exampleSpecs.stakes: punishing present safety for old danger
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Contrast an old interpretation of intimacy panic with a relational-map reading.

exampleSpecs.audience: caregivers learning why children protect unsafe adults
exampleSpecs.stakes: mistaking survival splitting for consent or loyalty
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Explain why a child may split awareness when dependence and danger live together.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers whose bodies distrust safe relationships
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show safety feeling foreign and mistreatment feeling familiar.

exampleSpecs.audience: group leaders responding to emerging memory
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Repair a moment where recognition was rushed instead of paced safely.
